research_mode: official Police.uk, Home Office and HMICFRS sources only; Force or BTP location semantics, current open-data references, national recording rules and inspection-cycle scope; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crime location-type contract
verified_claims: crime records expose a location_type field
the documented values distinguish Force and BTP locations
Force denotes a normal territorial police-force location
limitations: location type is not an offence category
the field does not establish exact incident coordinates

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: BTP and territorial-boundary overlap
verified_claims: BTP locations can fall within normal police-force boundaries
BTP and territorial-force records therefore have overlapping spatial contexts
location_type is needed to retain provenance
limitations: overlap must not be treated as duplicate proof without record-level keys
BTP coverage differs from territorial-force coverage

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: BTP location subtype
verified_claims: crime records expose location_subtype
the field describes the type of BTP location when applicable
it is distinct from the broader Force or BTP location_type
limitations: empty subtype is not a general missing-crime indicator
subtype must not be applied to territorial locations without evidence

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Latest outcome-status pair
verified_claims: crime records can include outcome_status
the status contains the latest recorded outcome category
it also contains the date of that latest outcome
limitations: latest status is not the complete case history
a missing status is not proof of no investigation

sources.name: Current police open-data update edition
verified_claims: the official open-data page records an update on 23 April 2026
the update refreshed multiple recorded-crime and outcomes products
edition date is part of current-source provenance
limitations: page update date is not the observation period for every table
individual files retain separate period and schema metadata

sources.name: Recorded-crime geographical reference
verified_claims: the open-data page publishes a recorded-crime geographical reference table
the reference is supplied separately from the main crime tables
geography mapping is an explicit supporting asset
limitations: reference geography is not parcel geometry
joins require edition-compatible codes

sources.name: Recorded-crime offence reference
verified_claims: the open-data page publishes a recorded-crime offence reference table
the reference table is separate from aggregate observations
offence-code interpretation depends on the reference asset
limitations: offence codes can change across editions
reference labels are not risk weights

sources.name: National crime-recording standard
verified_claims: the Home Office Crime Recording Rules provide a national standard
the standard covers recording and counting notifiable offences
the stated scope is police forces in England and Wales
limitations: a national rule does not guarantee identical local implementation
recording rules are not a parcel-safety methodology

sources.publisher: His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services
sources.name: PEEL force coverage
verified_claims: PEEL assesses police effectiveness efficiency and legitimacy
the programme covers all 43 police forces in England and Wales
force reports and grades are published through the programme
limitations: PEEL findings are inspection judgments rather than parcel observations
force-level assessment dates differ

sources.publisher: His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services
sources.name: Adaptive PEEL cycle framework
verified_claims: PEEL questions can change between inspection cycles
the framework adapts to changing policing priorities and circumstances
HMICFRS identifies a 2025 to 2027 cycle with its own methodology and questions
limitations: grades from different cycles require framework context
inspection judgments must not be converted directly into local safety scores
